newsitem.title: USA: AT&T's Allen says new CFO has Wall St savvy.
newsitem.headline: AT&T's Allen says new CFO has Wall St savvy.

text.p: AT&T Corp's chairman Robert Allen said Wednesday the company named Daniel Somers to the chief financial officer post in large part due to his Wall Street savvy.

Somers, who will take the post in mid-May, most recently was the chairman and chief executive of Bell Cablemedia Plc. Previously, he was CFO at Bell Canada International and served eight years as an investment banker and financial analyst.
"An important part of any CFO's job is to communicate with the Street...he knows his way around the Street and he's a good communicator," Allen said in an interview.
Allen, also chief executive, said the telecommunications company is facing a fast-changing marketplace and it needs a financial executive at the table who also has a strategic focus.
"We need a strong financial person at the senior level table who can think strategically, who can help us think through the various financial options," he said.

Somers will be one of four men in the chairman's office, the strategy center of the company. He joins Allen, president and chief operating officer John Walter, and senior executive vice president of corporate affairs John Zeglis.
Walter, who came to AT&T from R.R. Donnelly & Sons Co, is expected to succeed Allen as chief executive in 1998.
AT&T has said recently it is committed to opening the lines of communication with investors and analysts to improve frayed relations.
The company's stock, languishing recently near its 52-week low of 30-3/4, has been hammered by billions of dollars in writedowns over the last few years.
The company's shares closed Wednesday at 33-1/2, up 1/4 on the day.
